Housing Australia Amendment (Accountability) Bill 2025 - Second Reading - Agree with the bill's main idea
Housing Australia Amendment (Accountability) Bill 2025 - Third Reading - Pass the bill

Moved the Housing Australia Amendment (Accountability) Bill 2025, arguing that material changes to the Housing Australia Investment Mandate, including expansion of the Home Guarantee Scheme, should be subject to parliamentary oversight and disallowance; criticised delegated legislation and alleged declining Freedom of Information transparency, citing 25 per cent of requests fully granted under Labor.

Argued that the Housing Australia Amendment (Accountability) Bill 2025 would restore parliamentary oversight of ministerial changes to the Home Guarantee Scheme, which were said to have removed income and place limits and contributed to higher entry-level house prices; the debate also addressed delegated authority, transparency and disallowance.

Opposed the Housing Australia Amendment (Accountability) Bill 2025, arguing that allowing the Senate to disallow the five per cent deposit scheme, Help to Buy and the Housing Australia Future Fund would make homeownership and social housing harder, while supporters said the bill would restore parliamentary scrutiny of regulations.

Argued that the Housing Australia Amendment (Accountability) Bill 2025 would create uncertainty and obstruct affordable and social housing construction. Cited a Housing Australia Future Fund project of 171 affordable apartments in Rivervale and a pipeline of over 1,100 homes across Perth as evidence of current delivery.
